title: Hardship and Protective Holds: One Open Hold per Placed Account
content:
**Clause.** Under Hardship and Protective Holds a consumer may hold hardship holds on several placed accounts at once, but each placed account carries at most one open hold. A new hold request is taken only when no other hold on the same placed account is requested or active; a consumer who wants a different tier while a hold runs asks for it when the current hold ends, or ends the current hold first. No limit is set on the number of holds one consumer may hold across different placed accounts.

## What the clause tests

- **The object.** The test is made on the placed account the new request is for. Holds on the consumer's other placed accounts are not counted against it.
- **The evidence.** The test rests on the system's record of holds on that placed account and their status, as it stands before the request is taken. What the consumer says about earlier holds does not replace the record.
- **What counts as open.** A hold on the same placed account whose status is *requested* (an undecided request) or *active* (a running hold) is an open hold. Each request taken is recorded as a separate hold record of its own, dated with its own request date.

## Condition table

| Another hold on the same placed account | Is it an open hold under this clause? | New request on that account |
|---|---|---|
| Status requested | Yes | Not taken |
| Status active | Yes | Not taken |
| Status ended, denied or withdrawn | No | Not barred by this clause |
| No other hold on record | — | Not barred by this clause |

## Points of judgement

- *A consumer with a running hold asks for another tier on the same account.* The new request is not taken while the running hold is active. The consumer asks for the other tier when the current hold ends, or ends the current hold first.
- *A consumer with a running hold on one account asks for a hold on a second account.* The open hold sits on a different placed account, so this clause does not bar the request on the second account.
- *A consumer has holds on four different accounts.* No per-consumer limit applies; the clause looks only at whether each placed account already has an open hold.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A consumer has two placed accounts. Account A has an undecided request for a Documented Hardship Hold; account B has a hold that ended last month. A new request for a 30-Day Hardship Pause on account A is not taken, because account A already has an open (requested) hold. The same request on account B is not barred by this clause, because the ended hold on account B is not open.
